He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class. ==Early life and high school career== Livingston was born and raised in [[Akron, Ohio]].{{cite web |title=Chris Livingston |url=https://ukathletics.com/sports/mbball/roster/player/chris-livingston-2/ |website=UK Athletics |access-date=19 July 2025 |date=4 August 2022}}{{cite web |last=Thamel |first=Pete |authorlink=Pete Thamel |title=Meet Chris Livingston, the 14-year-old hoops prodigy LeBron James went out of his way to see |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/meet-chris-livingston-14-year-old-hoops-prodigy-lebron-james-went-way-see-013721817.html |publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=July 28, 2018}} He started playing competitive basketball at age five.{{cite web |last=Beaven |first=Michael |title=Freshman star Chris Livingston continues to develop alongside brother Cordell as Buchtel prepares for state tournament |url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/sports/20190320/boys-basketball-freshman-star-chris-livingston-continues-to-develop-alongside-brother-cordell-as-buchtel-prepares-for-state-tournament |website=[[Akron Beacon Journal]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=March 20, 2019 }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} As a freshman, he played for [[Buchtel Community Learning Center]] in Akron, averaging 24.7 points, 5.2 rebounds and 1.8 blocks per game. Livingston led his team to its first state final four appearance since 1997 and became the highest-scoring freshman in school history.{{cite web |last=Goul |first=Matt |title=Buchtel, Chris Livingston and Co. still learning after state final four run: 2019 preseason basketball tour |url=https://www.cleveland.com/highschoolsports/2019/11/buchtel-chris-livingston-and-co-still-learning-after-state-final-four-run-2019-preseason-basketball-tour.html |website=[[The Plain Dealer]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=November 20, 2019}} For his sophomore season, he transferred to [[Western Reserve Academy]] in [[Hudson, Ohio]].{{cite web |last=Beaven |first=Michael |title=Twin brothers Chris Livingston and Cordell Livingston transfer to Western Reserve Academy |url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/sports/20191129/twin-brothers-chris-livingston-and-cordell-livingston-transfer-to-western-reserve-academy |website=[[Akron Beacon Journal]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=November 29, 2019 |archive-date=January 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210124035840/https://www.beaconjournal.com/sports/20191129/twin-brothers-chris-livingston-and-cordell-livingston-transfer-to-western-reserve-academy |url-status=dead }} In his season finale, Livingston recorded 50 points, 20 rebounds, eight steals and five blocks in a 76–65 win over [[Bristol High School (Bristolville, Ohio)|Bristol High School]].{{cite web |last=Beaven |first=Michael |title=High school notebook: WRA's Chris Livingston ends season with 50 points in win over Bristol |url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/sports/20200224/high-school-notebook-wrarsquos-chris-livingston-ends-season-with-50-points-in-win-over-bristol |website=[[Akron Beacon Journal]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=February 24, 2020 |archive-date=February 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200225202317/https://www.beaconjournal.com/sports/20200224/high-school-notebook-wrarsquos-chris-livingston-ends-season-with-50-points-in-win-over-bristol |url-status=dead }} As a sophomore, he averaged 32.5 points, 12.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 2.9 steals and 1.4 blocks per game, earning [[MaxPreps]] Sophomore All-American first team honors.{{cite web |last=Helwagen |first=Steve |title=National top-five prospect Livingston hearing from key schools |url=https://247sports.com/college/ohio-state/Article/Ohio-high-school-basketball-prospect-Chris-Livingston-2022-hearing-from-Michigan-Wolverines-Ohio-State-Buckeyes-Kentucky-Wildcats-Texas-Longhorns-148225084/ |publisher=[[247Sports]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=June 15, 2020}} As a junior back at Buchtel, Livingston averaged 31.1 points, 15.8 rebounds, 6.1 assists, 4.7 steals and 4.0 blocks per game. He averaged 18.2 points, 9.1 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.9 steals per game during his senior season at [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]]. ===Recruiting=== Livingston was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services. He held multiple college basketball scholarship offers before entering high school. Livingston was offered by [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] at age 14.{{cite web |last=Goul |first=Matt |title=See Chris Livingston, nationally ranked freshman in Akron and Ohio State basketball target |url=https://www.cleveland.com/hssports/blog/2018/10/see_chris_livingston_nationall.html |website=[[The Plain Dealer]] |accessdate=July 27, 2020 |date=October 2, 2018}} On September 15, 2021, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] over offers from [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] and [[Tennessee State Tigers basketball|Tennessee State]].{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32215771/chris-livingston-commits-kentucky-giving-wildcats-three-five-stars-2022-basketball-class | title=Livingston becomes UK's 3rd 5-star commit in '22 | date=September 15, 2021 }} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2022}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Chris Livingston | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Akron, OH]] | highschool = [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] (VA) | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 200 | 40 = | commitdate = September 15, 2021 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 92 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2022 | rivals ref title = Kentucky 2022 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2022 Kentucky Wildcats Recruiting Class | rivals school = kentucky | scout s = | espn schoolid = 96 | 247 overall = 16 | rivals overall = 11 | espn overall = 12 | accessdate = March 25, 2022 | bball = yes }} ==College career== As a freshman at [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] in [[2022–23 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2022–23]], Livingston played in 34 games and made 26 starts, averaging 6.3 points and 4.2 rebounds in 22.4 minutes per game. He was named to the [[Southeastern Conference]] All-Freshman Team. ==Professional career== Livingston was drafted by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] as the last and 58th pick of the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite news|first=Dennis|last=Varney|title=Kentucky basketball's Chris Livingston headed to Bucks as final pick of 2023 NBA Draft|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article276598031.html|website=Kentucky.com|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=January 3, 2024}} On July 9, 2023, he signed a contract with the Bucks.{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks sign Chris Livingston|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-chris-livingston|website=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2023|access-date=January 3, 2024}} Throughout his rookie and sophomore seasons, he was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Wisconsin Herd]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Wisconsin Herd Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Wisconsin-Herd/50/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 18, 2024}}{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Wisconsin Herd Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Wisconsin-Herd/50/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 18, 2024}} Livingston made 21 appearances for Milwaukee during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 1.4 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 0.2 assists. After being waived by the Bucks on July 2, 2025,{{cite news |last1=Adams |first1=Luke |title=Bucks Waive Chris Livingston |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/07/bucks-waive-chris-livingston.html |access-date=19 July 2025 |work=hoopsrumors.com |date=2 July 2025}} he later re-signed with the team on July 16.{{cite news |title=Milwaukee Bucks Re-Sign Chris Livingston {{!}} Milwaukee Bucks |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-re-sign-chris-livingston |access-date=19 July 2025 |work=bucks.com |date=16 July 2025 |language=en}} Livingston was waived by the Bucks for a second time on October 16.{{Cite web|title=Bucks Cut Third-Year Forward Ahead of Regular Season|url=https://www.si.com/nba/bucks/news/bucks-cut-third-year-forward-ahead-of-regular-season|access-date=October 23, 2025|website=si.com|language=en}} On October 31, 2025, Livingston signed a two-way contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web | last=Franklin | first=Drew | title=Akron's own Chris Livington signs with Cleveland | website=KSR | date=2025-10-31 | url=https://www.on3.com/teams/kentucky-wildcats/news/akrons-own-chris-livington-signs-with-cleveland/ | access-date=2025-12-06}} He made three appearances for the Cavaliers, averaging 3.0 points, 1.0 rebound, and 0.3 assists. On January 27, 2026, Livingston was waived shortly after sustaining a hand injury that would keep him inactive for several weeks.{{Cite web|title=Cavs waiving two-way player|url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2026/01/cavs-waiving-two-way-player.html|website=cleveland.com|date=January 28, 2026}} ==National team career== Livingston played for the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in [[Belém]], Brazil. He led his team to the gold medal, recording 23 points, six rebounds and two assists in a 94–77 win over [[Canada men's national under-17 basketball team|Canada]] in the final.{{cite web |last=Beaven |first=Michael |title=Buchtel's Chris Livingston leads USA Basketball to 2019 FIBA Americas Men's U16 title in Brazil |url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/sports/20190610/buchtels-chris-livingston-leads-usa-basketball-to-2019-fiba-americas-mens-u16-title-in-brazil |website=[[Akron Beacon Journal]] |accessdate=July 27,
